title: Lut was one of the messengers.
subtitle: A messenger sent to a people who refused him
then: After Ilyas, the surah turns to Lut. Ibn Kathir says Allah sent His servant and messenger Lut to his people, {trap}and they denied him.{/trap} {idea}His rank came from being sent, not from being believed.{/idea}
now: You are the only one in your friend group who will not join in. You are the parent saying no when every other parent says yes. {idea}Standing for what is right does not need a majority.{/idea} Lut stood almost alone and Allah still called him one of the messengers.
old: If nobody listens to me, maybe I am the one who is wrong.
new: Being right with Allah does not depend on how many people agree.
try: Hold one small line today that you know is right, even if you are the only one holding it.

title: Allah saved him and his family, all of them.
subtitle: Rescue for those who stood with him

row.title: saved
sub: from among a people who denied

row.title: a whole town is lost
sub: so everyone in it is lost

then: Ibn Kathir says Allah saved Lut from among his people, {reward}him and his family{/reward}. Surrounded by a whole town that rejected him, he was not swept away with them. {idea}Allah knew exactly who stood with His messenger.{/idea}
now: You work at a company in trouble, live in a neighborhood going downhill, belong to a family with a bad name. {reward}Allah does not see you as a crowd.{/reward} He sees you, one person, and what you chose.
old: I will go down with whatever group I belong to.
new: Allah deals with me as a person, and He rescues those who hold on to Him.
try: Make dua today for your own household by name, one person at a time.

title: Except an old woman who stayed behind.
subtitle: Living with a prophet did not save his wife
then: Ibn Kathir says the old woman was Lut's wife, {trap}who was destroyed along with her people.{/trap} She shared a home with a messenger. {idea}She shared her heart with those who denied him.{/idea}
now: Your father prays at the front of the mosque. Your spouse is the religious one. You are in the WhatsApp group with all the good people. {idea}None of that is your faith.{/idea} Living near goodness is not the same as choosing it.
old: My family is religious, so I am covered.
new: Nobody's closeness to Allah can stand in for my own.
try: Do one act of worship today that is yours alone, not one you do because your family does it.

title: Then the rest were destroyed.
subtitle: The end of a people who refused
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah destroyed them with different kinds of punishment and turned their land into a foul lake. {trap}They had been warned, and they denied.{/trap} The story is told to the people of Makkah, {idea}who were mocking the same kind of warning.{/idea}
now: A bad habit you keep saying you will fix next month. A wrong you keep meaning to set right. {trap}Each day without consequence feels like proof it does not matter.{/trap} {idea}It is actually time being given to you.{/idea}
old: Nothing bad has come from this yet, so it must be fine.
new: The time before consequences is a mercy to use, not a sign that none are coming.
try: Name one habit you keep postponing. Do the smallest first step to change it today.

title: You drive past their ruins every morning.
subtitle: The lesson was on the trade route

row.title: a sign
sub: left there for them to read

then: Ibn Kathir explains the site was on a well-travelled route, the highway between Arabia and Syria, close to the Dead Sea. {idea}The people of Makkah passed it on their trade journeys.{/idea} The lesson was not hidden. {trap}It was on their commute.{/trap}
now: The hospital you drive past. The cemetery on the way to work. The friend's empty chair at the family dinner. {idea}Reminders are already in your route.{/idea} You only have to stop treating them as background.
old: I would reflect more if I came across something that made me think.
new: Allah has already put signs on my daily path. I just pass them without reading.
try: On your next commute, notice one thing that reminds you of death or of Allah. Pause on it for a breath.

title: And at night. Will you not think?
subtitle: Morning and evening, the same unread lesson

row.title: thinking
sub: learning that a like end awaits

then: Ibn Kathir explains the question: {idea}will you not learn a lesson from them{/idea} and realize that a similar end awaits those who deny? They saw the place day and night. {trap}They never connected it to themselves.{/trap}
now: You scroll past news of a sudden death at breakfast and again before bed. You say how sad, and keep scrolling. {idea}The verse asks you to stop and think.{/idea} What does this mean for how I live tomorrow?
old: I know life is short. I hear about death all the time.
new: Hearing about it is not the same as letting it change how I live.
try: Tonight, before sleep, ask yourself one question: if today were my last, what would I wish I had done?

title: Yunus was one of the messengers.
subtitle: A prophet whose story includes a slip

picture.label: The last story in the line

then: The surah now tells the story of Yunus. Ibn Kathir quotes the Prophet ﷺ in the Two Sahihs: {idea}it is not right for anyone to say I am better than Yunus bin Matta.{/idea} His story includes a slip, and {trap}the slip does not make him smaller.{/trap}
now: Someone you look up to messes up in public. A teacher, an imam, a parent. {trap}It is tempting to feel taller.{/trap} {idea}Their slip is not your rise.{/idea} The story of Yunus asks you to learn from it, not look down from it.
old: When a good person falls, it shows I am not so bad after all.
new: Someone else's mistake is a lesson for me, never a reason to rank myself above them.
try: Next time you hear of someone's failure, make a quiet dua for them instead of commenting.

title: He ran off to a ship already full.
subtitle: Leaving his post, onto a loaded boat

row.title: Allah is on every ship
sub: there is no away from Him

then: The verse says Yunus ran away, and the story calls what he did {idea}an act worthy of blame.{/idea} He boarded a ship that, as Ibn Abbas said, {trap}was filled with cargo.{/trap} A full ship, a storm coming, and a prophet away from his people.
now: The project gets hard, so you start updating your CV. The marriage gets tense, so you stay late at the office. The duty feels heavy, so you book a trip. {idea}Sometimes the hard place is exactly where Allah wants you.{/idea}
old: When things get too hard, the answer is to get out.
new: Before I run, I should ask whether Allah has released me from where I am.
try: Think of one place you want to escape from. Make dua for guidance before deciding anything.

title: They drew lots, and he lost.
subtitle: The storm, the overloaded ship, the draw
then: Ibn Kathir explains that the ship was being pounded by waves and at risk of sinking. {trap}They drew lots to choose who would go overboard.{/trap} Yunus lost the draw three times. The sailors did not want to throw him, but {idea}the decree kept pointing at him.{/idea}
now: You miss the train, lose the job offer, get the one test result you dreaded. {trap}It feels like the draw is rigged against you.{/trap} {idea}It may be Allah turning you back toward something.{/idea} Losing a draw can be the start of a return.
old: Things keep going wrong for me. I must just be unlucky.
new: When doors keep closing, Allah may be steering me somewhere I need to go.
try: Look at one recent setback and ask: what might Allah be turning me toward?

title: Swallowed by the fish, knowing he was at fault.
subtitle: The lowest point of the story

row.title: it is the end of me

then: Ibn Kathir says Allah commanded a great fish to swallow Yunus {idea}without cutting his flesh or breaking his bones.{/idea} The verse says he was blameworthy, {trap}he had done something deserving of blame.{/trap} Even inside the punishment, he was being kept safe.
now: You know the mess you are in is your own doing. The debt, the argument, the lie that grew. {trap}The weight of knowing it was you is the heaviest part.{/trap} {idea}Owning it is not the end. It is where the way out begins.{/idea}
old: I caused this, so I do not deserve a way out.
new: Admitting I am at fault is the first step out, and Allah can protect me even inside my mistake.
try: Say to Allah, in your own words, one thing you know you got wrong. Nothing more.

title: His glorification of Allah was his rope out.
subtitle: What he did in the good days saved him

row.title: I will pray when I need it
know Allah in ease
sub: He will know you in hardship

then: Scholars gave two meanings. Many, including Ibn Jarir, said it was {reward}the good he had done in times of ease.{/reward} Ibn Kathir quotes the hadith: remember Allah in ease and He will remember you in hardship. Others said it was his cry in the darkness: {idea}none has the right to be worshipped but You, glory be to You, I was a wrongdoer.{/idea}
now: Life is calm right now. Salary in, kids healthy, no hospital visits. {reward}This is the time to build the habit.{/reward} The dhikr you say on an easy Tuesday is the rope you will hold on a terrible Friday.
old: Things are fine at the moment, so I can relax my worship a bit.
new: The worship I do in easy times is what carries me when hard times arrive.
try: Pick one short dhikr and say it ten times today while things are calm.

title: Without it, the fish would have been his grave.
subtitle: How close the other ending was
then: The verse shows the other ending. {trap}He would have stayed in the belly of the fish until the Day of Resurrection.{/trap} Ibn Kathir quotes a report that the angels recognized his weak voice from a far place, because {reward}his good deeds used to keep rising to them.{/reward}
now: You are in a place with no exits you can see. The diagnosis, the debt, the court date. {trap}Every human door is shut.{/trap} {idea}One door does not need a key you hold. It opens from the other side when you call.{/idea}
old: If I cannot find a way out myself, there is no way out.
new: When every door I can reach is shut, calling on Allah is still a door.
try: In your hardest situation right now, say the words of Yunus once, slowly: La ilaha illa Anta, subhanaka, inni kuntu minaz-zalimin.

title: Thrown onto a bare shore, weak and sick.
subtitle: Rescued, but not yet restored
then: Ibn Abbas and others said the shore was {trap}land with no vegetation and no buildings.{/trap} Yunus came out weak of body. {reward}He was saved{/reward}, but the recovery had not yet begun.
now: You got out of the bad job, the toxic relationship, the hospital bed. {trap}You expected to feel amazing. Instead you feel empty and tired.{/trap} {idea}That is still rescue.{/idea} Lying on the bare shore is part of being saved.
old: If Allah really answered me, I would feel better by now.
new: Being brought out is the first answer. Healing can come after, slowly.
try: If you are recovering from something, give yourself one hour of rest today without guilt.

title: Allah grew a gourd vine over him.
subtitle: Shade and food on an empty shore

row.title: a simple plant
sub: exactly what a sick man needs

then: Many early scholars said the plant was squash. Ibn Kathir lists its benefits: {reward}it grows fast, its broad leaves give shade, flies avoid it, and its fruit nourishes.{/reward} {idea}Allah's care came as an ordinary plant, perfectly suited to a weak man on a bare shore.{/idea}
now: After the hard season, help arrives small. A neighbor brings soup. A coworker covers your shift. A friend sends a voice note at the right moment. {idea}That is the gourd vine.{/idea} Do not overlook it because it looks ordinary.
old: I am waiting for Allah to fix this in a big way.
new: Allah often sends care through small, ordinary things that fit my need exactly.
try: Notice one small kindness someone shows you today, and thank Allah for it by name.
